page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. This instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 236 GB local disk, and the server is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are positioned in the bottom tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4-2ads_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring substantial RAM but minimal parallel processing power. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage provides additional value for data-caching needs. This server is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, text processing, and small-scale development environments that do not require heavy multi-threaded compute.

Large-block memory bandwidth and small-model LLM inference speeds remain average. Qualitatively, this server provides high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a cost-efficient choice for memory-heavy, single-threaded workloads. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, text processing, and lightweight caching tasks that do not require extensive parallel processing.
